item.title: Some states are allowing lawsuits against federal agents. Is it a viable option?
item.description: Trump administration officials say federal agents have "total immunity," but a number of states have passed laws allowing them to be sued. But is it a viable option for those seeking accountability?

item.title: Andrew Tate is seeking bail in his extradition fight. Here's why that's unlikely
item.description: There's a fear that people facing international extradition granted bail could flee. Andrew Tate and his brother face a total of 59 criminal charges in the U.K., including rape and human trafficking.

item.title: NDAs are hiding data center deals, drawing ire from locals — and attention from lawmakers
item.description: Nondisclosure agreements covered up negotiations between a tech company and several local and state officials, surprising local residents. It's a tactic used around the country in data center deals.

item.title: Amid rising threats, a WNBA team calls in experts on violent extremism
item.description: The WNBA's popularity has risen in recent years, but so have threats and abuse directed at its players. One team is taking a novel approach to this, by partnering with national security specialists.

item.description: People in Sevierville, Tenn., remember their hometown girl, Dolly Parton — not only for her songs, but for her lifetime of generosity to the place she came from.

item.title: In Louisiana, NDAs covered up a data center deal that residents didn't know was coming
item.description: Residents of tiny Boyce, La., yelled at local officials for signing agreements that hid a pending deal for a data center. NDAs, common in Louisiana data center deals, are coming under more scrutiny.
